title: The perfect-family calculation on the Brown telescope
statement: Let C be a pretriangulated category, locally small in v, with all v-small coproducts. Let (S_j) indexed by a v-small type be closed under integer shifts up to isomorphism, and perfect: componentwise surjectivity on Hom from every S_j is preserved by v-small coproducts. Let H:C^op to Ab_v be additive. Let X_0 to X_1 to ... be a tower with compatible elements x_n in H(X_n). Suppose evaluation against x_0 is onto H(S_j) for every j, and every map S_j to X_n killed by x_n vanishes after the next transition. For a distinguished telescope triangle sum X_n --(1-shift)--> sum X_n --q--> T --r--> (sum X_n)[1] and an element t of H(T) restricting along each stage to x_n, evaluation Hom(S_j,T) to H(S_j) against t is bijective for every j.

source.place: Cellular Brown construction in Krause Derived categories, resolutions, and Brown representability Section 4.5, comparison with the telescope; the proof here expands this comparison using coproduct weak kernels and constant-sequence retractions instead of coherent functors.

proof.text: Coproducts of distinguished triangles give weak kernels for coproduct maps: pass to the opposite category, use productTriangle_distinguished and Hom exactness, and transport by opCoproductIsoProduct. Evaluate all generator maps into these weak kernels; perfectness lifts maps through the sum of the evaluation maps. Therefore, for maps b_i:W to Y_i pulling y_i back to a common z, any map S_j to a sum of copies of W killed by sum b_i is killed by sum c, provided c kills each generator map annihilated by z.

Let b_n:X_0 to X_n be the iterated transitions. Cover X_n by X_0 plus the coproduct of all generator maps annihilated by x_n, using b_n on the first summand. Initial surjectivity makes this map onto Hom(S_j,-). Perfectness lifts generator maps into sum X_n through the sum of these covers. The kernel summands die at the next stage.

A generator map fixed by the tower shift consequently factors through B:sum X_0 to sum X_n. Let s_0 and s_1 be the shifts on the constant sequences at X_0 and X_1 and A=sum a_0. The weak-kernel calculation shows (h-h s_0)A=0. Since s_0 A=A s_1 and 1-s_1 has the explicit retraction given on summand n by minus the sum of preceding inclusions, cancel 1-s_1 to get h A=0. Also s_1 has a left-shift retraction. Cancelling it and factoring s_0 B through A makes the original fixed map zero.

Shift closure transfers that injectivity to the shifted first telescope map. Exactness of Hom on the distinguished triangle now lifts every map S_j to T through q. The covers show every such lifted map factors through X_0 in T. Surjectivity follows from x_0. If evaluation of a map to T is zero, its X_0 factor is killed by a_0, so the map itself is zero. Apply this to the difference of two maps to obtain injectivity.

lean.statement:
theorem perfectFamily_telescope_bijective
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Preadditive C] [HasZeroObject C]
    [HasShift C ℤ] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive]
    [Pretriangulated C] [HasCoproducts.{v} C]
    {J : Type v} (S : J → C)
    (hshift : ∀ (j : J) (n : ℤ), ∃ k, Nonempty (S k ≅ (S j)⟦n⟧))
    (hperfect : ∀ (I : Type v) (X Y : I → C) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ Y i),
      (∀ i j, Function.Surjective (fun g : S j ⟶ X i ↦ g ≫ f i)) →
      ∀ j, Function.Surjective (fun g : S j ⟶ ∐ X ↦ g ≫ Limits.Sigma.map f))
    (H : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{v}) [H.Additive]
    (X : ℕ → C) (a : ∀ n, X n ⟶ X (n + 1))
    (x : ∀ n, H.obj (op (X n)))
    (hx : ∀ n, H.map (a n).op (x (n + 1)) = x n)
    (hsurj : ∀ j, Function.Surjective (fun f : S j ⟶ X 0 ↦ H.map f.op (x 0)))
    (hkill : ∀ n j (f : S j ⟶ X n), H.map f.op (x n) = 0 → f ≫ a n = 0)
    (T : C) (q : Telescope.sum X ⟶ T) (r : T ⟶ (Telescope.sum X)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hT : Triangle.mk (𝟙 _ - Telescope.shift X a) q r ∈ distTriang C)
    (t : H.obj (op T))
    (ht : ∀ n, H.map (Telescope.ι X n ≫ q).op t = x n) :
    ∀ j, Function.Bijective (fun f : S j ⟶ T ↦ H.map f.op t)
